why.box: A box is read to a tenth of a CSS pixel, a node's and a painted surface's alike (a surface's inside its node). One pixel lets a sub-pixel layout round either way; the smallest spacing token is 4 px, so a changed one is still caught. A step of one pixel is inside it by design: the drawn values say it where a node or its words carry it.
why.drawn: No tolerance: a drawn value is the browser's computed string and must be equal, on a node, on the words inside it and on every surface that paints. This is what makes one changed token red on any machine, also where the change is too small or too faint for a picture to show, and for a state whose picture nobody accepted. A face the reference's words are set in must have loaded: a face that did not arrive leaves the font-family string as it was. Everything painted says how it is turned, by one reading: of the matrix the browser puts it on the screen with, what is left when where it is and how large it is drawn are taken out, said as an angle, a mirror or, for a slant, the matrix. A node, its words, a surface, a box a stylesheet draws before or after an element and each shape of an icon say it. So a caret that is a bordered box pointing up for down is red here, and so is a line through a sign turned the other way or laid flat, a letter turned a quarter and a row's mirrored words; the same thing moved, zoomed, scrolled or at another device scale is not, and neither is one turn written another way or on another element around the thing. What stands upright says nothing. An icon says its fills and strokes, a stroke with its cap, join and dashes, and a digest of the shapes a person sees: each one's geometry and that matrix, read from the icon's middle in the icon's own units. Another icon of the same box, colour and stroke is red here in a row of any width, and so is the same icon turned or mirrored. Not read, and left to the picture, which fails on them for an accepted state by its mark line: what a clip, a mask, a filter or a blend mode does, what a gradient or a pattern holds, a marker, a picture that is no inline svg, a line under or through words and where words stand in their node (README.md, Known limits).
why.mark: The most differing pixels of an accepted state's picture that may touch one another, a corner counts: a mark, as a person reads one. A share does not hold a small mark: the reference's own caret pointing up for down moves 30 to 192 pixels of a screen, 0.0018 to 0.0065 of its region. The marks are read with every differing pixel in, an edge's too; the shares leave out what pixelmatch takes for a soft edge, and with it most of a thin stroke that moved (that caret is 8 pixels there and 44 here). The line is in the picture's own pixels and sits between two measurements. Two draws of one state: three pairs of draws of the reference, 7,034 pairs of pictures, 6,858 of them equal byte for byte; where the two show the same state, the largest mark is 11 pixels at a scale of one (the plus of a small icon rastered a part of a pixel apart, the same mark in ten states) and 3 at a scale of two. The smallest marks changed, on a made row of 420 by 72: a caret in 11 px type turned a quarter 23 pixels (63 at a scale of two), a check mark gone from its box 45, a check for a chevron 68, the line through a sign laid flat 85, which the drawn values read as well; and what only the picture can tell, 20 to 282 (a line through words, a clip, a marker, a gradient, a picture changed for another). Above the line in two draws are only states the reference lays out one of two ways (97 pixels and more: unsteady.json). Under it, and under the noise: one letter changed in small type (a full stop for a comma 6 pixels, i for l in 11 px type 2), which the names question reads, an 8 px picture moved inside its box (10), and a pattern of dots made bars (nine marks of 4).
why.pixel: pixelmatch counts a pixel whose YIQ distance is over 35215 × pixel², here 0.56. One step of every channel at once is 0.51 and does not count: that is what two machines may round a blend apart by. Anything more does: the design's own surface steps are all over it, in every theme (a sheet on the ground is 200, the unread tint on a sheet 102, a dark theme's hover on a sheet 35, the closest two, a dark theme's unread tint and its mark, 0.68). A test draws every surface of every theme and holds that the picture tells each two apart. pixelmatch leaves out pixels it takes for anti-aliasing, which keeps a soft edge that did not move from counting; it does not make a moved edge equal: letters half a pixel off count, and an accepted picture is the same picture, not a near one. Two draws of one page are the same picture at this line: of 1,565 states drawn twice, 1,520 are equal byte for byte, and the same number count a pixel at this line as at four times it.
why.pictureRatio: The share of the whole picture that may differ: the larger of 0.001 and three times the share measured between two machines on the own subjects. It fails a state whose picture was accepted. Between two draws on one machine the largest share of a state that shows the same state twice is 0.0004.
why.regionFloor: A node's region is grown to 12 CSS pixels a side, so the smallest mark is still read over an area and not over a handful of pixels.
why.settle: A picture is taken once the scene and every pixel are the same on two looks 600 ms apart. The design reference opens some states on a timer after its page loaded: with its motion shortened, the longest is 260 ms, and the latest change seen on a loaded machine came 520 ms after the load. Animations and transitions take no time, and a page's scripts wait for its fonts, so nothing is caught half way and text is never measured in a fallback font. Without all three, two captures of the same tag on one machine differed in 572 of 2,911 pictures, 232 of them by more than the picture's line. A page still changing after 8 s has no picture.
why.chromiumArgs: Hinting, LCD text and sub-pixel glyph positions are what a machine's font configuration changes; they are off on both sides. The colour profile is fixed to sRGB. Animations run on the main thread, not on the compositor's: on its own thread an animation that is already over is now and then drawn at a value on its way (a see-through layer one to four steps of a channel off in about one draw in fifty, and three times in 2,882 states a whole sheet half see-through), and the picture is then of no state the page was ever in; with the switch, 600 draws of two such states gave one picture each. The browser is the one Playwright pins, so a new Playwright is a new measurement (tolerance-pinned.test.ts).
why.regionRatio: The share of one node's region that may differ. A region is a small part of a picture, so its share for the same change is tens of times the whole picture's and has its own line: the larger of 0.005 and three times the worst region share measured between two machines. Of 1,565 states drawn twice on one machine, every one whose two draws show the same state stays at or under 0.0022 in its worst region; the seven over 0.005 are states the reference places differently from run to run (unsteady.json). A later reading of 942 states gave 0.0027 as the largest such share. At 0.005 the smallest region at a scale of one (144 pixels) lets no pixel differ; at a scale of two it lets two. A wide region lets a small mark change whole inside this line: a 16 px icon swapped for another is a four-hundredth of a 420 by 72 row (0.0025; 0.0014 at a scale of two). That is why what an icon is, is asked of the drawn values, and why an accepted picture also has a mark line.
why.grossRatio: Over this share of the whole picture, any state fails, accepted or not: a picture that differs in a fiftieth of its pixels shows another screen, not a near one. Under it, a state whose picture nobody accepted reports.
why.clock: A clock read twice in one run of script reads the same (render.mjs). The reference prints how long its calendar search took; without this, fifteen states read other words on every draw.

measuredOn.workstation: The five own subjects drawn twice: no pixel differs. The reference drawn twice from its tag with this renderer, 1,565 states of ten screens, held together with all four questions: 1,520 equal in picture and data file, 38 differ and are green (worst region 0.0022, whole picture 0.0004), 7 are red and are states the reference itself draws differently from run to run (unsteady.json). Before animations were kept on the main thread and the clock was held within a run of script, the same reading over all 2,882 states gave 22 red: fifteen search states that print a measured time, three sheets drawn half see-through, and four of those seven. When the reader learned an icon's shapes the whole set was drawn again, and ten screens a second time. The two whole sets, 2,882 states, with the new readings taken out: 2,849 equal on all four questions with no pixel counted, 25 differ and are green, 8 are red, five of them named before and three new in unsteady.json. The two draws by the new reader, 1,075 states: 1,073 data files equal byte for byte, no drawn value differs, and the 5 red are all named. When the reader learned where the browser puts each shape of an icon, turned or mirrored, the whole set was drawn once more and thirteen screens a second time. The two whole sets with the new readings taken out: 2,842 equal on all four questions with no pixel counted, 32 differ and are green, 8 are red, seven of them named before and one new in unsteady.json. The two draws by that reader, 942 states with 15,926 icons: 940 data files equal byte for byte and the two others are named states; no ink differs but in one of those two; the 5 red are all named. When every painted thing learned to say its turn and the picture its marks, the whole set was drawn once more and seventeen screens a second time. The two whole sets with the new readings taken out: 2,822 equal on all four questions with no pixel counted, 53 differ and are green (largest mark 11), 7 are red, five of them named before and two new in unsteady.json. The two draws by that reader, 2,076 states: 2,072 data files equal byte for byte and the four others are named states; no turn and no generated box differs between the two draws, and no ink but in three states of the letter that turns read; the 12 red are all named, five of them new. Six states were named in all, each red by a mark of 106 to 2,731 pixels and green on every share but one: words or a card placed a pixel of the device apart on a foldable.
measuredOn.runner: Not measured yet: no job runs the comparison. The own pictures were taken on a workstation; the job's first run reads the share that differs there. pictureRatio and regionRatio stay at their floors until then, and each becomes three times its measured share if that is more; the mark line is read there too, and moves above the largest mark two machines draw of the own subjects if that is more. The two accepted own subjects carry no text, so that reading says nothing about letters: a subject set in the bundled faces belongs to the change that brings the font files.
